subject.title: Feature: Subscribe to WhatsApp call events (Baileys)

question: Should inbound WhatsApp call activity be exposed, and if so should it be a sanitized plugin hook, session/contact activity state, an agent tool query, or some combination?
rationale: The missing Baileys listener is clear, but the permanent surface controls sensitive call metadata and may add config, retention, and plugin/agent API behavior that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Default-off minimal activity event
options.body: Add a WhatsApp-plugin-owned listener that emits sanitized call activity only after explicit opt-in and avoids storing raw call metadata by default.

options.title: Hook-only first step
options.body: Expose a trusted `call_received`-style plugin hook with privacy gating, but defer agent memory/session state until the contact-activity model is designed.

options.title: Defer inbound calls
options.body: Keep this open or close as not planned until a broader WhatsApp activity/privacy model exists.

recommendation.title: Default-off minimal activity event
recommendation.body: Add a WhatsApp-plugin-owned listener that emits sanitized call activity only after explicit opt-in and avoids storing raw call metadata by default.

likelyOwner.reason: He recently scoped this issue in comments and authored the adjacent WhatsApp call-tool direction, so he is the best available product/security routing owner from the inspected history.
